subject: ent
title: Facial nerve and its disorders

steps.tx: The **facial nerve** exits the pons, traverses the internal meatus and temporal bone (labyrinthine, tympanic and mastoid segments), gives greater petrosal, stapedial and chorda tympani branches, then exits the stylomastoid foramen to supply facial muscles, stapedius and taste to anterior tongue. Its long bony canal explains vulnerability to ear disease and temporal fractures.
steps.say: Facial nerve winds through ear bone supplying face movement, stapedius and front tongue taste. Ear disease and fractures threaten it.

steps.tx: **Bell palsy** is acute idiopathic lower motor neuron facial paralysis (forehead included) reaching peak within days, likely herpetic inflammation swelling the nerve in its tight labyrinthine segment. Early corticosteroids within 72 hours improve complete recovery; antivirals add debated benefit, and eye protection (lubrication, taping) prevents corneal damage when closure fails. Most recover well.
steps.say: Bell palsy weakens the whole face including forehead, peaking fast. Early steroids help; protect the open eye.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Lower versus upper motor neuron signs separate urgently: forehead sparing means central (stroke) because forehead receives bilateral cortical input, while forehead involvement means peripheral nerve lesion. Ramsay Hunt adds vesicles and worse prognosis; Lyme, sarcoid, parotid tumours and otitis cause secondary palsies needing cause treatment, not Bell label.
steps.say: Forehead spared means brain lesion; forehead weak means nerve lesion. Blisters, lumps or ear infection mean not simple Bell palsy.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Temporal bone fractures paralyse by segment: longitudinal fractures (commoner) tear along the bone often with conductive loss and CSF otorrhoea, while transverse fractures cross the labyrinth causing sensorineural loss, vertigo and higher facial palsy rates. Delayed palsy (oedema) recovers better than immediate (transection). Surgical decompression or repair is selected by electrophysiology and imaging in specialist care.
steps.say: Transverse temporal fractures deafen sensorineurally and paralyse more; longitudinal cause conductive loss and CSF ear leak.

steps.tx: Grading uses **House Brackmann** scale I (normal) to VI (total paralysis) for prognosis and trials. Incomplete eye closure risks exposure keratitis needing ophthalmology. Aberrant regeneration later causes synkinesis and crocodile tears (gustatory lacrimation) when fibres regrow to wrong targets. Chronic palsy rehabilitation includes gold weights, static slings and botulinum for synkinesis.
steps.say: Grade palsy I to VI. Guard the cornea first. Late rewiring causes linked movements and tears while eating.
